mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > (current value + 0.25%) in the following month
regime_hint: Rising FED Funds rate after a period of lowering
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite FEDFUNDS increase, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a backtest.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PAYEMS (labor market activity) of at least 2% over two months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as hiring momentum supports corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >= 2% over the next two months
regime_hint: Expanding labor market with rising employment
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 60-day window despite the labor signal, or the effect is explained by other variables (e.g., inflation).

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (goods demand) grows faster than CPIAUCSL (inflation) over the next quarter, S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days are expected to be positive, reflecting stronger real demand.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > CPIAUCSL growth rate over next 3 months
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day return when the condition holds, or the effect is reversed in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 5% in a month predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as a signal of weakening manufacturing momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in the following month
failure_condition: Positive 5-day forward returns when INDPRO declines sharply, or the effect is not statistically robust.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent FEDFUNDS above 5%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to higher real rates compressing equity valuations.
regime_hint: High FED Funds rate steady regime
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or equal to the risk-free rate in this regime.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3.5% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is predicted to be positive as lower unemployment suggests economic resilience.
regime_hint: Low unemployment or easing labor market
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 60 days despite the UNRATE signal.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST (household spending) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 4% over the next 20 days predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return, reflecting strong consumer and retail demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >=4% AND RSAFS increases by >=4% over next 20 days
regime_hint: Strong consumer and retail demand acceleration
failure_condition: No significant return when both proxies rise as specified.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO and GDPC1 both show a double-dip decline (each >2% drop in consecutive months), the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be negative, reflecting persistent supply-side weakness.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >2% in month X and GDPC1 falls >2% in month X+1
regime_hint: Consecutive declines in key supply indicators
failure_condition: Positive 60-day returns when the double-dip pattern occurs.
